findings.problem: The chosen product investigates processor, bank, and accounting exports, but the proposed scenarios and success criteria never establish an observable accounting-side investigation. A Stripe-to-bank implementation could satisfy every listed scenario while merely accepting an unused accounting CSV.
findings.remedy: Add one synthetic accounting-side discrepancy with a stated observable outcome and include the accounting source in the demonstrated evidence journey. State the accounting export's role in the first slice; exact fields and matching rules can remain for architecture review.

findings.problem: The design requires preserving and reproducing an approved report, but the core journey only saves a reviewer disposition and generates a report. Neither the journey nor the conceptual review/report states explains what action approves the report or when its immutable snapshot becomes fixed.
findings.remedy: Choose the conceptual approval boundary: state whether saving a disposition also approves a case/report or whether approval is a separate action, and identify when the report snapshot becomes immutable and how a subsequent correction starts a new reviewable version. Exact transitions and database contracts can remain for architecture review.
